Understand electrochemistry through classification

Secondary batteries overview

Batteries that reverse chemical reactions through charging for repeated use. Different names use different classification criteria.

Charging & dischargingClassification of namesLithium-ion cathode familiesOther secondary batteries

What is reversed during charging?

During discharge, electrode reactions send electrons through the external circuit to supply power. During charging, an external source drives the reaction in reverse to store energy again. Ions move through the electrolyte to maintain charge balance.

DischargeChemical energy → electrical energy
ChargeElectrical energy → chemical energy
Repeated useLosses and degradation accumulate

Rechargeable does not mean unlimited life. Electrode and electrolyte side reactions, structural changes, temperature and operating conditions reduce capacity and power over time.

Are all secondary batteries named after the cathode?

LFP, NMC (NCM), NCA, LCO and LMO name the cathode active material of lithium-ion batteries. This rule does not apply to every secondary battery. Cathode materials form the positive electrode, and these abbreviations specifically identify the active material participating in energy-storage reactions.

Classification axisExample namesWhat changes?
Cathode active materialLFP·NMC/NCM·NCA·LCO·LMOLithium-ion energy density, voltage, stability and material composition
Anode active materialLTO (lithium titanate)LTO replaces graphite as the anode; it can be paired with cathodes such as NMC or LMO
Mobile ion / chemistryLithium-ion, sodium-ion, lead-acid, nickel-metal hydrideBasic energy-storage chemistry
Electrolyte state / compositionAll-solid-state / lithium-polymerAll-solid-state uses solid electrolytes; lithium-polymer relates to electrolyte and cell construction
Storage / circulation structureFlow batteriesElectrolytes are stored in external tanks and circulated through the reaction unit
Cell formatCylindrical, prismatic, pouchShape and packaging, separate from cathode chemistry
Several names can apply simultaneously. For example, LFP cathode + graphite anode + liquid electrolyte + prismatic cell describes four different elements. Solid-state cells may use LFP or NMC cathodes. Flow batteries can be recharged and therefore belong to secondary batteries.

Representative lithium-ion cathode families

FamilyCathode active materialKey features & challenges
Lithium iron phosphate · LFPLithium iron phosphate · LiFePO₄Stability and long life without nickel or cobalt. Generally lower energy per unit mass than NMC.
Nickel manganese cobalt · NMCNickel–manganese–cobalt oxideHigh energy density. Properties depend on composition; nickel/cobalt supply and thermal management matter.
Nickel cobalt aluminum · NCANickel–cobalt–aluminum oxideHigh energy density; thermal management, charge control and material supply matter.
Lithium cobalt oxide · LCOLithium cobalt oxide · LiCoO₂Widely used in small electronics; cobalt cost and safety management are challenges.
Lithium manganese oxide · LMOLithium manganese oxide · typically LiMn₂O₄Power capability and manganese-based materials are strengths; life and high-temperature performance remain challenges.

NMC and NCM name the same nickel–manganese–cobalt family. NMC811 indicates an 8:1:1 relative molar ratio of nickel, manganese and cobalt. Cathode names alone cannot determine life, cost or safety; assess the anode, electrolyte, design and use conditions as well.

Secondary batteries beyond lithium-ion

FamilyKey featuresMain applications
Lead-acid batteriesCompetitive price and established recycling; heavy with low energy densityVehicle starting and backup power
Nickel-metal hydride · NiMHNickel-based cathode and hydrogen-storage alloy anode; relatively mature technologyHybrid vehicles and everyday rechargeable cells
Nickel-cadmium · NiCdDurability and temperature tolerance; consider cadmium toxicity and regulationIndustrial backup power
Sodium-ion · Na-ionUses sodium ions; material choice and resource accessibility are strengthsESS and selected vehicle development / commercialization
Sodium–sulfur · NaSSodium–sulfur chemistry; high-temperature operation requires insulation and safety managementLarge-scale electricity storage
Vanadium flow battery · tank circulationVanadium electrolytes circulate from tanks; power and stored energy can be sized relatively independentlyLong-duration ESS
Zinc–bromine flow battery · tank circulationZinc–bromine chemistry; circulating designs are flow batteries. Zinc deposition and bromine management matter.Stationary ESS
